title: p256-ecdlp: negation-map parallel Pollard rho with doubling escape (v3)

claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r), input Q=[x]P on NIST P-256, recover x. Before submitting, we read this track's current best accepted submission (5fa78d6, Meganpark980320) and independently re-verified its key finding: additive escape on a fruitless rho collision traps a large fraction of long trails in a persistent cycle (we measured 35/150=23% on our own construction), while doubling escape (X<-[2]X, exploiting that small integers have enormous multiplicative order mod r) traps 0/150 in the same test. This revision switches to doubling escape, charged at an empirically-measured (4.07%) escape rate with a generous 10% bound; targets success probability 0.40 (explicit margin over the 0.39 floor); and uses a chaining hash table (not open addressing with a probe cap) to avoid a per-operation-vs-whole-attack overflow-probability mismatch a sibling submission's review flagged. Total computation is at most 5.423512e+38 reference-group-operation equivalents (borrowed C=1,000). A dependency on 5fa78d6 is declared for the doubling-escape and explicit-margin insights; the cost ledger, table structure, and escape-rate derivation are independently derived and verified.

experiments.purpose: Exhaustively check the production mechanism exactly: W parallel walks, mixed c_h/d_h branch points, sign canonicalization, a shared chaining table checked on every step, DOUBLING escape (not additive) on fruitless collisions, linear-solve. Reports escapes_triggered and escape_rate, with escapes counted in total_steps. Does not validate production curve arithmetic, instruction costs or full-size timing.
